newsitem.title: USA: Apache, Seagull stress Egypt plans.
newsitem.headline: Apache, Seagull stress Egypt plans.

text.p: Apache Corp plans to spend $150-200 million developing oil and natural gas concessions in Egypt this year, chairman Raymond Plank said in a statement after a meeting with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Houston.
"Apache plans to drill 62 wells in Egypt this year, two-thirds of which will be exploratory wells," Plank said.
Seagull Energy Corp chairman Barry Galt said that 70 percent of its 1997 $100 million capital budget outside the U.S. would be spent in Egypt.
Apache is the largest leaseholder in Egypt, with interests in more than 27 million acres.
Seagull has interests in 9.3 million acres.

Apache and Seagull are partners in Egypt's Qarun and East Beni Suef concessions and the offshore Darag block at the northern tip of the Gulf of Suez. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
